# Solving the model

## Overview
`ems_solve()` solves the constrained optimization problem according to a range of runtime configuration options.
In order to solve, a teems Docker [image](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-solver) must be prebuilt.
Singularity, accuracy, and error checks are carried out following a successful run.
By default, solver outputs are automatically parsed into structured R objects via [`ems_compose()`](compose.qmd).

## Arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `cmf_path` | | Path to the CMF file generated by [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd) |
| `solution_method` | `"Johansen"` | Solution method (see below) |
| `matrix_method` | `"auto"` | Matrix solution method (see below); `"auto"` chooses from the model type, size and measured structure |
| `n_subintervals` | `1L` | Number of subintervals for the applied shock. More subintervals may alleviate accuracy issues stemming from large shock magnitudes |
| `steps` | `c(2L, 4L, 8L)` | Strictly increasing vector of three step counts for the `"Gragg"` and `"Euler"` methods. For `"Gragg"` all three must additionally be even (required by the method's extrapolation theory; Pearson 1991); `"Euler"` has no parity requirement. The Runge-Kutta methods take a single step count instead (e.g. `steps = 8L`) |
| `adaptive` | `"no"` | Adaptive step-size control for the embedded Runge-Kutta methods (`"BoSha32"`, `"DoPri54"`): `"yes"` redoes steps whose worst accuracy metric exceeds `eps_tolerance` (or on which a percentage-change variable crosses `-100%`) with a smaller step size and adjusts the next step size after every accepted step; `"accuracy-only"` acts on the accuracy metric alone |
| `eps_tolerance` | `0.1` | Per-step accuracy-metric bound targeted by `adaptive` control; `0.1` suffices for most simulations, `0.01` for high accuracy. Values below `0.005` are hard to achieve numerically |
| `n_tasks` | `1L` | Number of tasks to run in parallel. Must be `1L` if `matrix_method` is `"LU"` |
| `pre_probe` | `FALSE` | When `TRUE`, run the solver's structural probe first and abort with the defective variable and equation elements named if the deployed system is structurally singular (see [`ems_probe()`](#checking-solve-quality)). With `matrix_method = "auto"` the same probe run also supplies the structural evidence for the method choice |
| `suppress_outputs` | `FALSE` | When `TRUE`, solver outputs are not automatically parsed with [`ems_compose()`](compose.qmd) |
| `terminal_run` | `FALSE` | When `TRUE`, exits without running the solver, allowing the user to close R and run from the terminal |
| `...` | | Additional named solver arguments: the Runge-Kutta step controls (`max_retries`, `retry_adjust`), the MA48 workspace initial guesses (`laA`, `laD`, `laDi` — normally left unset: the solver sizes its workspace automatically, growing it as needed and warm-starting repeat runs from the recorded `la_used` in `sol.stats.json`) and the expert solver flags (`fastrefac`, `gpzerodivide`, `cntl_3`, `cntl_6`, `nsbbdblocks`, `withmc66`, `smllthreads`, `tempdir`, `nowrites`, `condest`, e.g. `smllthreads = 2L`). Unknown names are an error, never a silently ignored flag |

## Basic usage

```r
outputs <- ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "Johansen",
  matrix_method = "LU"
)
```

## Solution methods

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `"Johansen"` | Fast one-step approximation. Should only be used as a rough approximation due to handling of nonlinear equations. See [GEMPACK manual](https://www.copsmodels.com/gpmanual.htm#gpd1.2.13) |
| `"Gragg"` | Gragg's method (the smoothed modified midpoint method; Pearson 1991): the shock is applied over multiple linearized passes whose solutions are combined by Richardson extrapolation for improved accuracy. The `steps` parameter controls the per-pass step counts. See [GEMPACK manual](https://www.copsmodels.com/gpmanual.htm#gpd3.12.2) |
| `"Euler"` | The forward Euler method with the same three-solution Richardson extrapolation. Converges more slowly than `"Gragg"` (one order gained per extrapolation solution instead of two) but is the most robust multistep choice: each step uses only the current state, so it tolerates variables approaching asymptotes and severe shocks — including exact `-100%` shocks — where the midpoint family can become unstable. See [GEMPACK manual](https://www.copsmodels.com/gpmanual.htm#gpd3.12.2) |
| `"RK2"`, `"RK4"` | Explicit Runge-Kutta methods (the midpoint method and the classic fourth-order method; Schiffmann 2022). A single solution is computed with one step count — no Richardson extrapolation — each step built from 2 or 4 staged linear solves. `"RK4"` reaches a given accuracy in far fewer steps than the extrapolating methods |
| `"BoSha32"`, `"DoPri54"` | Embedded Runge-Kutta pairs (Bogacki-Shampine 3(2), 4 stages; Dormand-Prince 5(4), 7 stages). Alongside the solution they estimate the cumulative error of every variable element — returned as the `error_metric` column by [`ems_compose()`](compose.qmd) and summarized as a face value (10 = best) in the solver log — and support adaptive step-size control via `adaptive` and `eps_tolerance`. `"DoPri54"` with `adaptive = "yes"` is the recommended high-accuracy choice |

## Matrix methods
Increase `n_tasks` to take advantage of parallel matrix solution methods.
<!-- Add links to matrix method papers -->
| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `"auto"` | The default. `"SBBD"` for intertemporal models; `"LU"` for static models, switching to `"DBBD"` when `n_tasks >= 2`, the deployed system is large (roughly 2 million or more equations, or 1.5 million with 100+ diagonal blocks) and the solver's structural probe of the deployment finds a block partition with at least `n_tasks` blocks and a border below a tenth of the system. The probe is skipped when the deploy metadata already settles the choice (static single-task runs, static systems below 1.5 million equations); when it runs, its evidence and the thresholds used are reported and written to `model_diagnostics.txt`. Thresholds are calibrated on 1-4 task benchmarks; the `"SBBD"` to `"NDBBD"` escalation is disabled until measured. Set the method explicitly to override |
| `"LU"` | Standard LU decomposition. The most robust and potentially slowest for large models. `n_tasks` must be `1L`. Works with both static and dynamic models |
| `"DBBD"` | Doubly bordered block diagonal. Parallel matrix solution method for static models only. Potentially faster than `"LU"` although less robust |
| `"SBBD"` | Singly bordered block diagonal. Parallel matrix solution method for intertemporal models only. Potentially faster than `"LU"` although less robust |
| `"NDBBD"` | Nested doubly bordered block diagonal. Parallel matrix solution method for large intertemporal models with many timesteps only |

## Multi-step solution

For greater accuracy, use the Gragg method with subintervals:
```r
outputs <- ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "Gragg",
  matrix_method = "LU",
  n_subintervals = 2,
  steps = c(2, 4, 8)
)
```

Or an adaptive embedded Runge-Kutta run, which controls its own step
sizes against `eps_tolerance` and reports a per-element accuracy
estimate (subintervals do not apply — the controller replaces them):
```r
outputs <- ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "DoPri54",
  matrix_method = "LU",
  steps = 4,
  adaptive = "yes"
)
outputs$dat$qgdp$error_metric
```

## Memory parameters

If the solver returns "Error return from MA48B/BD because LA is ...", increase the relevant memory parameter gradually:

- `laA` applies to `"LU"` and `"SBBD"` methods
- `laD` applies to `"DBBD"` and `"NDBBD"` methods
- `laDi` applies to the `"NDBBD"` method only

```r
outputs <- ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "Johansen",
  matrix_method = "LU",
  laA = 500L
)
```

## Checking solve quality

If a model solves but the results look implausible — percent changes orders of magnitude too large, or accuracy figures that will not settle — the cause may be numerical rather than structural. `ems_probe()` catches wrong closures (variables nothing determines, equations that determine the same variable twice), but a model can be structurally perfect and still be numerically degenerate, typically when the closure depends on base-data flows that are very close to zero.

`condest = TRUE` measures every linear solve and reports it:

```r
outputs <- ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "Gragg",
  matrix_method = "LU",
  condest = TRUE
)
```

Each solve logs a backward error (how faithfully the system was solved) and the scaled condition numbers `kappa_w1`/`kappa_w2` (how sensitive the answer is to the data). Run maxima are recorded in `sol.stats.json` and appear in the model diagnostics. Read `kappa_w2`: values around `1e8`–`1e9` are ordinary for CGE Jacobians, while values approaching `1e15` trigger a warning that the system is numerically near-singular and its solutions are unreliable — the signal to look for near-zero flows your closure depends on, or to rerun with `precision = "f64"`.

The diagnostic never changes results — solutions are identical with it on or off — and it costs a few percent of solve time. It applies to the `"LU"` matrix method (the bordered methods warn and ignore it), and reports nothing for a zero shock, where there is nothing to measure.

## Parallel solving

For models that support parallel matrix methods, increase `n_tasks`:
```r
outputs <- ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "Johansen",
  matrix_method = "SBBD",
  n_tasks = 4
)
```

## Terminal mode

For long-running models, `terminal_run` allows the user to close any R IDE prior to running from the terminal:
```r
ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  solution_method = "Johansen",
  matrix_method = "LU",
  terminal_run = TRUE
)
```

## Solving in-situ

`solve_in_situ()` calls the [teems-solver](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-solver) directly with user-supplied input files, bypassing the [`ems_data()`](data_load.qmd) / [`ems_model()`](model_load.qmd) / [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd) pipeline.
The model file will be parsed but all input files must be provided in their final form.
No checks or modifications are applied to input files.

This function is intended for users who wish to use the teems solver with pre-prepared input files, or in combination with the standard pipeline by reusing the files written to disk by [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd).
If all input files already reside in `model_dir`, no copying is performed; otherwise files are copied into `model_dir` before solving.

### Arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `...` | | Named arguments corresponding to input files necessary for an in-situ model run. Names must correspond to "File" statements within the model Tablo file. Values correspond to file paths where these files are found |
| `model_dir` | | Base directory where input files will be copied if not already present, and model outputs will be written |
| `model_file` | | Path to the model Tablo (.tab) file |
| `closure_file` | | Path to the closure (.cls) file |
| `shock_file` | | Path to the shock (.shf) file |
| `solution_method` | `"Johansen"` | Solution method: `"Johansen"`, `"Gragg"`, `"Euler"`, `"RK2"`, `"RK4"`, `"BoSha32"`, or `"DoPri54"` |
| `matrix_method` | `"LU"` | Matrix solution method: `"LU"`, `"DBBD"`, `"SBBD"`, or `"NDBBD"` |
| `n_subintervals` | `1L` | Number of subintervals for the applied shock |
| `steps` | `c(2L, 4L, 8L)` | Vector of steps for the Gragg method |
| `n_tasks` | `1L` | Number of tasks to run in parallel. Must be `1L` if `matrix_method` is `"LU"` |
| `pre_probe` | `FALSE` | When `TRUE`, run the solver's structural probe first and abort with the defective variable and equation elements named if the deployed system is structurally singular (see [`ems_probe()`](#checking-solve-quality)). With `matrix_method = "auto"` the same probe run also supplies the structural evidence for the method choice |
| `suppress_outputs` | `FALSE` | When `TRUE`, returns the CMF file path instead of parsed outputs |
| `terminal_run` | `FALSE` | When `TRUE`, exits without running the solver |
| `solver_args` | `NULL` | Named list of the additional solver arguments `ems_solve()` accepts through `...` (the MA48 workspace initial guesses and the expert solver flags, e.g. `list(smllthreads = 2L)`); a list because the in-situ `...` carries the input files |

### Input files

All model-declared input files as well as `model_file`, `closure_file`, and `shock_file` are required.
Input files are passed as named arguments via `...`, where each name must correspond to a "File" statement in the model Tablo file.
For GTAP-RE, the Tablo file declares:

```
File GTAPDATA # base data file;
File GTAPINT  # intertemporal data file;
File GTAPPARM # parameter file;
File GTAPSETS # set file;
```

These names are then used as the named arguments to `solve_in_situ()`.
```r
solve_in_situ(
  GTAPDATA = file.path(write_dir, "teems", "GTAPDATA.txt"),
  GTAPINT = file.path(write_dir, "teems", "GTAPINT.txt"),
  GTAPPARM = file.path(write_dir, "teems", "GTAPPARM.txt"),
  GTAPSETS = file.path(write_dir, "teems", "GTAPSETS.txt"),
  model_dir = "~/in_situ_run/",
  model_file = "GTAP-RE.tab",
  closure_file = "GTAP-RE.cls",
  shock_file = "a_shock_file.shf",
  solution_method = "Gragg",
  matrix_method = "SBBD",
  n_subintervals = 1L,
  n_tasks = 1L
)
```

### Output modes

By default, `solve_in_situ()` returns a tibble containing model output variables and coefficients.
If `suppress_outputs = TRUE`, the function returns the CMF file path instead, which can be passed to [`ems_compose()`](compose.qmd) for manual parsing.
